Colombia–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty (2005, in force 2007)
Colombia–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (2008, in force 2010)

Andean Community Decision 291 (Andean Pact Foreign Capital Regime)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creates UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006 (anti-terrorist financing); Ley 2155 de 2021 (Social Investment Law) and Decreto Reglamentario 830 de 2021 (UBO registry and reporting to DIAN); Decreto 1071 de 2015 (FATCA IGA); Circular Externa 009 de 2017 of the Superintendence of Companies (SIC) for AML/CFT anti-money-laundering and anti-terrorist-financing systems of supervised entities, and applicable UIAF Resolution rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Certificate of Incorporation of the parent/shareholder (for non-resident juridical entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the Shareholder's Country of Origin (e.g., Companies House, HK Registry, Singapore ACRA)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registry or Tax Authority in the Shareholder's Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for the incorporation representative / legal holder
Shareholders' Passport / Foreign Identity Document (for all ultimate beneficial owners)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized Passport Office or Notary in Country of Origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Certified Notarial Attestation (depending on source-country treaty)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Franchise Agreement and Royalty Licenses (excerpts) for evidence of commercial substance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed in a non-Hague jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory universal PEP (Politically Exposed Persons) screening, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list screening, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List screening, EU Consolidated Sanctions List screening, and Colombian National Assets Confiscation and Laundering List (SINACOF) through UIAF-validated vendor tools. Screening must be performed on all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, franchisees, and ultimate beneficial owners immediately after UBO identification and re-run quarterly or upon any change in ownership. Negative and false-positive hits require escalation and refusal of incorporation until cleared by an independent compliance officer; enhanced due diligence applies to non-resident ownership in high-risk jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) operated by Confecámaras and local Cámaras de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, Medellín, or Barranquilla); online pre-application via the Chamber of Commerce virtual office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be written in Spanish/Latin-script alphabet. If the business uses a non-Latin or English brand name (e.g., 'BOBA TEA'), a direct Spanish transliteration or an easily readable phonetic version is required. The name must include a distinctive expression, must not be significantly identical to an existing registered trademark or corporate name, and must comply with the Chamber registry's 'nomenclatura' doctrine of single identity. Foreign-word trademarks are permissible if rendered in Latin characters and clearly distinct within the Colombian corporate names registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Alimentos y Bebidas (if implying certification not yet granted)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are valid for 30 calendar days from issuance. Extensions may be requested before expiry for an additional 30 days by filing a formal written request with the same Chamber of Commerce where the reservation was made. Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative recourse ('recurso de reposición') within 30 calendar days of notification, stating the grounds of appeal, attaching a legal name-conflict analysis. If rejected after the reconsideration, the applicant may proceed to avail of the contentious-administrative jurisdiction process before the Consejo de Estado. The reservation, extension, and appeal filings require a nominal fee (approx. USD 8–15) payable through the Chamber's online platform.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional acceptance: A virtual office address is permissible for administrative and correspondence purposes only if it is in the same municipal jurisdiction as the main operating premises, the registered address is publicly accessible to receive official legal notifications (service of process), and the S.A.S. maintains a physical 'domicilio' at the franchise's principal operational location where the corporate books and assets are physically kept. Foreign-controlled and franchise companies are expected to show a brick-and-mortar place of management (plant, warehouse, or commissary) for substantive presence and tax domicile. For the boba tea franchise (ISIC 5610), the registered office address must coincide with the location of the branded beverage outlet or the administrative head office if the franchise operates multiple outlets; a purely co-working virtual mailbox without a staffing footprint is not accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_5_Percent_Annual (unannounced on-site inspections by the Superintendence of Companies and local health/consumer safety authorities are unlikely in the first fiscal year, but probability rises to 15% if the company declares a virtual office or fails to report annual financial statements; food safety inspections by SIC and Ministry of Health are separate and occur with higher frequency at the operating venue rather than the registered office).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial name pre-reservation and issuance of certificate of name availability (Cámara de Comercio)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Decree 1075 of 2019, Article 3.2.2.3; actual fee varies by city, approximately USD 10–15

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of S.A.S. bylaws and incorporation deed (Escritura Pública) by a Colombian attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for S.A.S. incorporations with drafting; notary fees are regulated by Auto-Notarial tariffs (approx. USD 50–90 per deed)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the incorporation deed and issuance of notarial folio (Notaría Pública)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee table (2001–2024 tariff range, approx. 0.3% to 1% of authorized capital; fixed minimum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration in the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and filing with the Mercantile Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Medellín / local Chamber
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tariff fixed by Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) under Resolution 0580 of 2022; based on capital amount and industry code, USD 80–150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and Sworn Spanish translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National/State Apostille Authority (in origin country) and Certified Translator (Colombia)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille fees per parent-country (USD 5–50), official Spanish translation by a sworn translator (Colombia: USD 150–300 per page set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (Beneficiario Final) initial registration filing with DIAN under Decree 830 of 2021
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for the online UBO filing; however, a compliance officer fee of USD 100 applies if delegated to external counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for AML/KYC onboarding, PEP and sanctions screening, and document verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard hourly or fixed for AML/CFT due diligence package (USD 200–400)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation municipal food safety / operating license (candidate location review and endorsement) — stage 1 hold deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alcaldía Municipal / Secretaría Distrital de Salud
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Preliminary municipal endorsement fee for location feasibility and zoning check; actual license fee is triggered at Stage 2 and varies with municipal tariff (USD 50–250)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Código de Comercio, arts. 98-116, 372, 374; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de la jurisdicción del domicilio social; Registro Único Empresarial (RUES); Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for NIT and RUT
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución S.A.S. (private incorporation document), certified by the Chamber of Commerce; Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for S.A.S.; capital may be subscribed in authorized shares and paid in cash or non-cash assets. No escrow account is legally required, but the bylaws must stipulate the term for payment of subscribed shares, and any actual disbursement must be deposited in a Colombian bank account as documented by bank certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators have duly subscribed the authorized capital of the company as set out in the bylaws, representing one hundred percent of the subscribed shares; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be established at the address designated in the bylaws, and said office shall be used for statutory notices and corporate administration; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed to office: President and General Manager, Secretary, and Statutory Auditor. The officers so appointed shall have the powers and duties provided by the bylaws and Colombian law, and shall immediately execute all documents necessary to register the company and obtain all operating licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability and Fiscal Capacity Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or competent local Chamber of Commerce) via RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a free name search application (Certificado de Homonimia) through the Chamber's online platform or in-person window. Request a certificate confirming no identical or confusingly similar trademark or corporate name exists. This certificate is valid for 30 days and is required before registration.
required_dossiers: Completed name search form
Identification document of applicant or authorized legal representative
Power of attorney if acting through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected due to similarity, file a new name search with a distinct corporate name, or request a reasoned derogation from the Chamber of Commerce after providing evidence of legitimate trademark difference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Private Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The incorporator or legal counsel; notarization only required if in-kind assets are contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución S.A.S. containing corporate purpose, capital set-up, share classes, board structure, registered office, term, and statutory auditor provisions. The incorporators must sign the document. If capital is contributed via real estate or other assets requiring public deed, the document must be granted before a Notario Público.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all founding shareholders
Draft bylaws / private incorporation document
Detailed valuation report and public deed for in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry objects to the document, amend the bylaws and resubmit within the correction period. In case of substantive legal defects, execute a new private incorporation document and cancel the prior filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de la jurisdicción del domicilio social (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed private incorporation document to the Chamber of Commerce along with the name certificate and prescribed fees. The Chamber will register the company into the Registro Mercantil, issue the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation, and thereafter assign a NIT (tax identification number) if not already assigned. The registration process includes the payment of registration tax and Chamber fees.
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución
Valid name availability certificate
Identification documents of shareholders and initial officers
Proof of payment of Chamber registration fees
RUT draft and NIT assignment form (if not already obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a deficiency notice or rejects the registration, correct any omissions within 10 days and file a formal response. If the rejection concerns the corporate purpose, expand or clarify the business activities and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – RUT Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Chamber has registered the company and provided the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation, register the company with the DIAN to obtain the NIT. File the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) electronically through the DIAN portal or at a service window. Request an electronic invoicing authorization and determination of the applicable tax regimes (income tax, VAT, withholding obligations).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Shareholders' identification data
Proof of registered office address (utility bill or lease)
Completed RUT forms on DIAN portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN queries the RUT, respond through the electronic portal or attend the assigned DIAN office to correct data, presenting updated incorporation documents. If the assigned tax classification is incorrect, file a reconsideration request with supporting statutory evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a Corporate Bank Account and Deposit of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Colombia (any registered credit institution) and the Chamber of Commerce for capital certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name. Deposit the subscribed capital (or the proportion due under the bylaws) and secure a bank certificate stating the amount deposited. The bank certificate is required for certain administrative and licensing procedures. Inform the Chamber if the capital is fully paid within three years or as scheduled in the bylaws.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
NIT and RUT
Identification of legal representative and signatories
Bylaws
Initial capital deposit form and bank remittance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the opening due to KYC/AML queries, provide enhanced due diligence documentation (source of funds, corporate chart, ultimate beneficial ownership declarations) and reapply. If the deposit amount does not meet the bylaws, amend the payment schedule by shareholders' resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Registro Mercantil) and DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the 'Formulario de Registro de Actividades Económicas' and submit the commencement of business notice (Solicitud de Inscripción de Impuestos y Actividades Económicas) before starting operations. For restaurant/franchise activities, also register the specific ISIC 5610 activity code and request the local transit and zoning certificates. This step formalizes the company as active for tax and commercial purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
RUT with economic activities endorsed by DIAN
Proof of bank account and capital deposit
Franchise agreement or licence contract, if applicable
Fiscal address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber or DIAN rejects the commencement form due to missing information, replenish the form and attach a corrected RUT. If the commencement notice is challenged, file an amendment through the RUES portal before the registry activates the status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría de Salud municipal / Departamental and Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA) for food safety; Alcaldía or District Mayor's Office for operating permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Alimentos y Bebidas (Sanitary Registration) and Certificado de Condiciones Sanitarias / Licencia de Funcionamiento for food service operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for projects of national character; for local premises, the municipal environmental authority or Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for regional matters
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or Registration tier for food and beverage retail/franchise operations unless central production of syrups generates wastewater above threshold; a full EIA is not required for low-impact beverage dispensing and packaging but a municipal environmental impact certificate may be required for commercial activity modification
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015 for maximum allowable limits of BOD5, COD, TSS, oils and greases; VOCs and particulates, if any, must meet Resolución 909 de 2008 air emission standards; solid waste handling must follow Decreto 4741 de 2005, including hazardous waste classification for used cooking oil and chemical cleaning agents, and franchise stores must implement waste separation and collection plans

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos (fire brigade) certifying fire extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke detectors, and evacuation plan; structural load inspection certificate and uso de suelo (land use compatibility) from the local Alcaldía/Planeación; and workplace clearance from the ARL (Aseguradora de Riesgos Laborales) registering employees and mandatory occupational risk prevention program

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – National Tax and Customs Directorate of Colombia; taxpayer portal: MUISCA (https://muisca.dian.gov.co); official site: https://www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Colombian S.A.S. obtains its NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) at incorporation through the Chamber of Commerce Single Registry (RUE). The NIT is also the VAT ID; no separate VAT-ID suffix exists. The company must then complete/update its RUT (Registro Único Tributario) before DIAN and activate the applicable tax responsibilities: income tax (declarante del impuesto sobre la renta), IVA responsible (responsable de IVA), withholding agent (agente de retención), and electronic invoicing (facturador electrónico). For a foreign entity itself acquiring Colombian tax registration, the non-resident must appoint a local agent/representative and file the RUT/NIT application before DIAN using apostilled or legalized constitutional documents (translated to Spanish by an authorized translator); registration must precede the first invoice or tax return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Colombian check-the-box or US-style fiscal-transparency election is available; an S.A.S. is mandatorily taxed at entity level and cannot be treated as a pass-through/partnership. The only elective regime of practical relevance is the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación' (SIMPLE), a turnover-limited consolidated income/IVA/municipal tax regime for qualifying small businesses; it is not an entity-classification or hybrid-mismatch election. No hybrid mismatch elections exist for outbound royalty or syrup-export structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Colombian Value Added Tax / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None in Colombian pesos for legal entities; the S.A.S. is a mandatory IVA responsible from the first taxable act. There is no economic-turnover registration threshold for companies. The statutory de-minimis non-responsible status, where still applicable, is limited to natural persons under the UVT-based turnover limits and is unavailable to a corporate franchise/supply-chain entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory end-to-end electronic invoicing via the 'Factura Electrónica de Venta' regime: every local B2B/B2C invoice must be generated in DIAN-authorized software, digitally signed, assigned the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica), and transmitted in real time to DIAN's MUISCA/Sede Electrónica platform for prior or posterior validation. B2B sales require electronic acceptance (acuse de recibo); export invoices must match the validated customs export declaration. Physical fiscal stamping is not used in Colombia; DIAN's digital validation operates as the clearance and control mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods (bubble-tea syrups, packaging, ingredients) qualify as 0% IVA exports when legal ownership passes to a non-resident buyer and the goods are physically exported from Colombian customs territory. Services (franchise royalties, brand licensing, technical assistance, software development, digital customer service) qualify as 0% IVA export services when rendered from Colombia to a non-resident, economically used outside Colombia, and not embedded in Colombian taxable transactions. The Colombian S.A.S. retains full right to recover input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports. For royalty flows from foreign franchisees, the zero-rating is available only where substance, transfer-pricing, and export documentation demonstrate a true cross-border export service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX/Formulario Único de Exportaciones) transmitted via DIAN/VUCE
Commercial invoice issued by the Colombian exporter
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from Colombian customs territory
Transport/customs documentation endorsed to the Colombian exporter and foreign buyer records
Declaración de cambio (foreign-exchange declaration) and inward remittance certificate/bank collection evidence showing repatriation of export proceeds within the mandatory 180-day period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits export zero-rating refund claims by matching the export declaration, transport documents, customs exit validation, foreign buyer identification, FX repatriation, and books/records. Missing or inconsistent documentation causes outright rejection of the 'saldo a favor' (VAT refund balance). If a refund was previously paid, DIAN will claw it back retroactively plus default interest and may impose tax-inaccuracy penalties (sanción por inexactitud), improper-refund penalties, and corporate debarment from electronic-refund programs; fraudulent schemes trigger criminal tax-fraud liability under Colombian law. The general assessment/statute-of-limitations window is five years from the statutory filing deadline, with extended exposure where criminal fraud or related-party offshore concealment is alleged.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting in coordination with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and the DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) under Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, and Resolución 8 de 2000 (Régimen de Cambios Internacionales y de Comercio Exterior), as updated by Circular Reglamentaria Externa DCIN-83 and Decree 1192 of 2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed-float exchange regime in which the COP is fully convertible within the 'mercado cambiario' (authorised foreign-exchange market). Current-account transactions—including franchise royalties, brand-license fees, syrup imports, and dividend payments—are freely channelable through licensed commercial banks and authorized exchange houses without prior administrative approval, provided each transfer is documented in the applicable Declaración de Cambio filed by the intermediary. The capital account is open for unrestricted sectors, and the retail food-and-beverage franchise activity is unrestricted; however, foreign direct investment must be registered in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales maintained by Banco de la República to preserve the statutory right to repatriate capital and remit profits. Profit remittance by the Colombian S.A.S. to non-resident shareholders is legally unblocked once (i) the corporate income tax (35% headline rate) is settled, (ii) the non-resident dividend withholding (7.5% under Article 242 E.T.) is discharged, and (iii) the foreign-exchange operation is declared under the appropriate causal code. There are no FX quotas, priority lists, or auction mechanisms restricting convertibility for legitimate franchise-treasury flows; the practical hurdles are documentary (apostilled corporate records, Spanish translations, UBO declarations) rather than regulatory. Derivative operations are permitted solely for genuine commercial hedge purposes; speculative merchant-level positions are subject to SFC sanction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Resolución 8 de 2000 (Articles 78–84 for goods; Article 106 and related for services), as simplified by Decree 1192 of 2020, the Colombian S.A.S. exporting franchise services, know-how licensing, and syrups must channel 100% of the export proceeds through the authorised 'mercado cambiario' within 6 months from the date of shipment (goods) or from the invoicing/service-provision date (services). The statutory obligation is 'canalización y declaración'—routing hard currency through a licensed intermediary and filing the exchange declaration (Form 1 for goods exports; Form 2 for services/royalties)—not compulsory conversion to COP: the exporter may retain USD/EUR in a foreign-currency account at a local commercial bank or, in specifically authorised cases, in a 'cuenta de compensación' abroad. The intermediary must lodge the declaration with Banco de la República within 5 business days of settlement, generating the Certificado de Cambio that constitutes the legal evidence of channeling. Extended collection terms (up to 18 months for certain goods) require prior application to Banco de la República or the authorised intermediary under the general regime. For the boba-tea franchise, each royalty and franchise fee receivable from foreign franchisees must appear in the S.A.S. receivables ledger with a matching commercial invoice, and the related FX must be channeled and declared within the 6-month window; failure triggers the exchange-regime sanctioning framework (multas cambiarias) applied by the SFC or DIAN.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente/Cuenta de Ahorros) plus segregated USD-denominated capital-receiving account
Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) and Capital Contribution Receiving Account
Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente / Cuenta de Ahorros) with USD current-account capability
Operational Account and FX settlement account
Operational Account with international correspondent rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for substantive treasury operations; MEDIUM only as an auxiliary wallet for non-COP, non-Colombian flows. Colombia's FX regime requires all foreign-exchange transactions of Colombian residents to be settled through authorised exchange intermediaries (commercial banks, financial corporations, and authorized exchange houses). Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer, Revolut Business) are not licensed Colombian exchange intermediaries: they cannot file the Declaración de Cambio, cannot issue the Certificado de Cambio, and cannot register foreign investment with Banco de la República. A Colombian S.A.S. receiving franchise royalties or capital injections through an offshore EMI would breach the mandatory channeling rule, leaving the funds without the exchange-declaration formalities required for the 6-month surrender/channeling timeline and exposing the company to SFC/DIAN exchange sanctions and tax-evasion presumptions. The correct architecture is to restrict offshore EMI usage to upstream group treasury (e.g., receiving payments from non-Colombian sub-franchisees that have no Colombian nexus and where funds never enter COP accounts), while all legally required Colombian-leg flows—capital injections, royalty final receipt, profit remittance—must route through a tier-1 local bank with full exchange documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default expectation for non-resident shareholders and legal representatives of a newly incorporated S.A.S. opening a corporate bank account at a tier-1 Colombian bank. In practice, Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, and BBVA Colombia will require at least one in-person interview at a Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali branch for the legal representative and, in enhanced-due-diligence cases, for the ultimate beneficial owner, unless a fully remote onboarding with video-KYC is pre-approved by the bank's compliance committee. Since the issuance of the SFC's digital-onboarding guidance, remote opening is permitted for standard-risk operations, but for a foreign-owned S.A.S. the bank typically mandates: (i) an apostilled and notarised power of attorney (poder especial) translated into Spanish by a certified interpreter; (ii) a live video call showing passports, constitutional documents, and the parent's certificate of good standing; and (iii) certified bank statements evidencing the provenance of initial capital. Recommendation: schedule a 2–3 day on-site visit to Colombia to execute the account contract, register authorised signatures, and complete the 'Registro de Firmas'; treat remote onboarding only as a fallback with an expected 2–4 week longer timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners and a multi-level offshore holding chain (e.g., regional IP holder in Netherlands/Singapore above the Colombian operating S.A.S.)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-control diagram covering 100% of the equity cascade; apostilled constitutional documents for every holding entity; certified UBO declarations (Declaración de Beneficiario Final, DIAN format 447 and internal bank forms); shareholder background summaries; audited consolidated financial statements for the last two years; and bank references evidencing the lawful origin of the group's capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border royalty flows with no visible economic nexus in Colombia (franchise fee/receipt mismatches)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed franchise and license agreements (licencia de marca, know-how, supply-chain); DIAN and customs records; a transfer-pricing support study (Estudio de Precios de Transferencia) filed with DIAN; per-invoice support for each royalty; and the Certificados de Cambio with the corresponding NIO reference numbers evidencing lawful channeling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or abrupt capital injection shortly after incorporation (indicative of round-tripping or suspicious structuring)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' assembly minutes approving the capitalisation; source-of-funds evidence (12+ months bank statements of the contributing shareholder); Colombian inbound FDI exchange declaration with the causal code for 'inversión directa en el país - aportes de capital'; and the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales certificate issued by Banco de la República.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive retail activity inconsistent with a declared franchise-licensing and syrup-supply model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: S.A.S. treasury policy limiting local collections to recognised POS rails; monthly EPOS/BMS reconciliations; DIAN sales declarations and IVA (19%) returns matching cash deposited to tax-filed revenue; and an internal policy prohibiting excessive cash structuring ('estructuración de efectivo').

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparties in FATF-listed or INCSR-watched jurisdictions within the franchisee or supplier payment circuit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial due-diligence reports on each flagged counterparty; UBO declarations of franchisees; FATCA/CRS self-certifications under the group's tax-compliance framework; contractual anti-money-laundering covenants; and the completed enhanced-due-diligence questionnaire accompanied by local counsel's legal opinion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for wiring equity into the Colombian S.A.S.: (1) Parent board/shareholders' resolution approving the capitalisation; (2) USD remittance via SWIFT MT103 to the S.A.S.'s USD-denominated account at the tier-1 bank, with beneficiary named exactly as the Colombian entity (including the NIT), Field 70/72 referencing 'Aportes de capital - Inversión Extranjera Directa S.A.S. NIT [xxx]'; (3) the receiving bank settles the operation in the 'mercado cambiario' and files the Declaración de Cambio (Formulario No. 3) using the causal code for foreign direct investment capital contributions ('inversión directa en el país - aportes de capital', section 2000 series of the Banco de la República causal-code table per Circular DCIN-83); (4) the investment must be inscribed in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales through the intermediary, producing a registration code that is mandatory for future profit remittance and capital repatriation; (5) no prior government authorisation is required for the unrestricted bakery/beverage service sector, but if trademark or know-how is capitalised as an in-kind contribution, an independent valuation and DIAN transfer-pricing support are required; (6) if the parent elects to inject a shareholder loan instead of equity, the disbursement must be registered as a 'crédito externo' with Banco de la República and declared under the external-debt causal codes—equity injection is legally simpler and recommended at Stage 4; (7) the S.A.S. must maintain an internal 'matriz de canalización' tracking the Certificado de Cambio of each injection against the 6-month channeling deadline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the boba-tea franchise treasury: (a) Royalty and franchise-fee payments to the global brand owner or regional headquarters are executed by SWIFT MT103 through the tier-1 Colombian bank's correspondent network, supported by the DIAN withholding-tax certificate (retención en la fuente rates for royalties/technical services as per the applicable tax treaty or the Colombian Internal Tax Code) and by the exchange declaration filed with the causal code for 'servicios y regalías' (3000/4000 series of the causal-code table); (b) syrup, cup, and ingredient imports are settled via commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 (MT700/MT707), with documentary compliance requiring bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and INVIMA import authorisation for food-grade boba ingredients, with payment mechanics via MT754/MT400 through the issuing bank; standby letters of credit (MT760) are used for franchise-bond and supplier-security obligations; (c) domestic operational disbursements—payroll, local suppliers, and DIAN tax payments—run through the CENIT ACH rail and the PSE online-payment gateway, while boba-store sales settle through the bank's POS acquiring infrastructure; (d) every outbound cross-border payment leg must be mapped in the treasury dashboard to its supporting contract, invoice, transfer-pricing file, and Certificado de Cambio reference to satisfy the 6-month channeling verification and DIAN/SFC audit readiness.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP forward contracts ('contratos forward de cobertura') executed with authorised local banks (Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, BBVA Colombia, Davivienda) under bilateral ISDA or local master-derivative documentation, limited to forecast royalty receivables and import payables.

Non-deliverable USD/COP forwards (NDFs) with international bank counterparties for offshore hedging of non-Colombian sub-franchise cash flows, documented with a hedge-designation memo evidencing the underlying commercial exposure.
USD/COP cross-currency swaps and currency-interest-rate swaps with local banks for medium-term treasury restructuring of intercompany funding and equipment-import disbursements.

USD/COP currency options (calls and puts) acquired from authorised intermediaries, strictly limited to firm commercial exposures and prohibited for speculative positions by the S.A.S. treasury policy.
USD/COP currency futures traded on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (regulated futures segment) for transparent exchange-rate risk management and margining efficiency.

Natural hedging through multi-currency accounts (USD/EUR/PEN/MXN) and strategically timed pre-payment or early settlement of trade payables, which requires no derivatives authorisation and is preferred for smaller ticket volumes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil – annual renewal of the commercial registration through the RUES portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Chamber of Commerce) via the national RUES online system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 covering the immediately preceding calendar year; no staggered extension for entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extemporaneous-renewal surcharge, loss of clean-standing certificate, inability to formalize acts before notaries and the Chamber; repeated non-renewal may trigger SIC cancellation of the matrícula mercantil

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (Impuesto sobre la Renta y Complementarios, Article 240 E.T., as in force for fiscal year 2023 onward)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
